title: Latency variance visual skein - ops playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, operational-first playbook for surfacing and triaging high-latency variance incidents across the inference stack. The focus is on synthesizing a small, high-signal dashboard set plus tracing anchors that make handoffs from on-call -> infra -> runtime teams fast and deterministic.

Why "visual skein"?
We use "visual skein" to describe a small set of correlated visualizations (heatmap + ribbon + breadcrumb trace links) that together show where latency spread is happening (tenant vs route vs token-path). The skein is intentionally narrow: operator can open a single page, scan 3 panels, and pick next actions.

Signal inventory (short):
- p50/p95/p99 request latency (ms) by model and route (rollup = weighted by token count)
- latency variance (ms^2) and coefficient of variation (stddev / mean) per-tenant, per-route
- token-path tail latency: distribution of per-token generation time for long responses (>256 tokens)
- kvcache-warmth delta: fraction of requests that hit prefix cache within a session window
- fallback-rate: percent of requests that fell back to cheaper/older model variant
- synthetic-probe-latency: periodic probe per-region/model/route (1m cadence)
- queue-time and scheduling-wait (ms): time spent waiting for a GPU slot
- model-load-time (ms): cold-start time for model variants

Metric definitions (explicit)
- request_latency_ms: elapsed_ms from HTTP request recv to final token emitted (exclude streaming ack). Aggregation: p50/p95/p99 over 5m windows. Tag by model, route, tenant_id, region, capacity_tier.
- latency_variance_ms2: sample variance of request_latency_ms over 5m window. Use Welford online algorithm to avoid numeric issues.
- latency_cv: sqrt(latency_variance_ms2) / max(1, request_latency_mean_ms). Reported as percent.
- token_step_time_ms: per-token span duration measured from token-gen start -> token-gen end; aggregated to distribution and percentiles
- kvcache_warmth_pct: (requests_with_kvcache_hit / requests_with_session_context) * 100 over 5m
- fallback_rate_pct: (requests_using_fallback / total_requests) * 100 over 5m

Important measurement rules
- Always populate tenant_id when available; store an anonymized tenant_hash for privacy in dashboards.
- For multi-model fanout, attribute latency to the slowest downstream model (max) and also emit per-branch latencies. Rollup panels show max latency while heatmap drilldowns show branch contributions.
- Streaming responses: if last_token_delta > 2s, record both streaming_interruption flag and per-token pause spans.
- Synthetic probes must be treated separately from production requests; separate metrics namespace and separate alert thresholds.

Trace anchoring and sampling strategy
- Anchor traces at request entry and at token-gen microcalls. Two span groups: handler-spans (HTTP, auth, routing) and model-spans (model_inference, kv_cache_read, kv_cache_write, scheduler_wait).
- Sampling: severity-weighted adaptive sampling. Rules: always sample 100% of traces where request_latency > p99_expected OR fallback_rate triggered OR synthetic_probe_failure. For noise reduction, sample 1% of p50 requests and 5% of p95 requests by tenant weighting.
- Trace naming: use stable span names: model_inference, kv_read, kv_write, scheduler_wait, gpu_copy, call_fallback. Add attributes: model_version, quantization_profile, batch_size, seq_len, tenant_hash.
- Trace link anchors on dashboard panels: include short trace ids and a "replayable request" hash (for prompt replay) when allowed by data classification.

Dashboard composition (visual skein)
Panel A - Variance heatmap (top-left)
- x-axis: time (1m steps), y-axis: routes (grouped by model family). Each cell color = latency_cv percentile (e.g., median of per-route CV for window). Click cell -> open Panel B filtered.

Panel B - Ribbon: p50/p95/p99 over selected route or tenant
- Stacked ribbon showing p50 (band), p95 (edge), p99 (outline). Overlaid: synthetic-probe-latency as dotted line. Goal: operator sees whether p95 change moved the whole distribution or only tail.

Panel C - Token-step sparkline + token-path heatmap
- Shows per-token generation time distribution for a sample stream (top offenders) across percentiles. Useful when p99 is driven by long tail token stalls.

Panel D - Trace anchors and top traces
- List of top 10 sampled traces for the selected time window, with precomputed blame tags (kvcache_miss, scheduler_wait_high, model_variant_fallback). Each row has brief timings and a link to trace viewer + GitHub PR if a regression is suspected.

Panel E - Operator checklist & quick actions (UI affordances)
- Buttons: warm-kv-cache (kick synthetic warms), re-route-to-fallback, scale-up-pool, pin-model-version, create-inc (prefill template).

Triage flow (operator)
1) Look at heatmap: identify routes/tenants with increased CV or variance spikes.
2) Open ribbon for that route: did p50 shift or only p95/p99? If p50 shifted -> broad regression. If p99 only -> tail issue.
3) Check token-step sparkline: are token stalls visible? If yes -> kvcache/prefix or scheduler contention.
4) Open traces: identify blame tags. If kvcache_miss dominates -> kick warm/cold cache repro. If scheduler_wait_high -> check pool utilization and queue-time panels.
5) Apply quick action (scale-up or pin-model) and annotate incident.

Runbook snippets (copyable)
- Quick repro for kvcache miss: run probe with recent session context and use --session-hash=<sample> to reproduce prefix behavior.
- Scheduler hotfix: temporarily increase capacity_tier for affected pool, monitor p95 over 2 minutes, then roll back.

Open questions / follow-ups
- How much cardinality for tenant_id is acceptable before dashboard query cost spikes? Propose: 1% sampling for detailed per-tenant panels, rollup-only otherwise.
- Should trace retention tier for sampled high-tail traces be extended to 90d for model-rollback investigations?
- Can frontend add per-panel quick-action to warm kv cache for a specific tenant? (UX + security)

Next steps
- Prototype the visual skein in dashboards sandbox (work item INF-4217). Omar -> spike visual wireframe by 2025-03-07.
- Implement adaptive sampling config in tracing service (Maya + Tomás).
- Draft SLO-level thresholds for variance-based alerts (product + SRE).

Notes to self / ephemeral ideas
- Consider adding a "variance anomaly score" that mixes absolute delta, CV, and synthetic-probe divergence. Could reduce noise compared to simple p99 alerts.
- Keep playbook < 3 clicks from oncall page to action: heatmap -> ribbon -> trace -> action.

References and links
- Design spec (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OBS/INF-visual-skein-design
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/814

End of doc.
